companies.companyThesisPath: 04 Thesis/Company/AAOI - Applied Optoelectronics AI Optics Thesis.md

profileSummary.oneLiner: Applied Optoelectronics supplies optical networking components and modules, giving it levered exposure to data-center bandwidth demand and telecom/cable cycles.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: AAOI benefits directly from the explosive growth in AI-driven data center buildout requiring ever-higher speed optical transceivers (400G, 800G, 1.6T). Their vertical integration — from in-house epitaxial growth of lasers, to component assembly, to full transceiver modules — provides cost advantages, faster iteration, and supply chain control compared to fabless peers. Recent major customer wins with Microsoft (2023 supply deal) and Amazon (2025 share option/purchase deal) signal validation from hyperscalers. As p...
keyRisks: History of operating losses and high volatility in stock price tied to capex cycles.
Intense competition from larger, more diversified players (Broadcom, Coherent, Lumentum, Acacia/Cisco, Chinese suppliers).
Customer concentration risk — reliance on a few large hyperscalers and cable MSOs.
Manufacturing execution in scaling advanced 200G/lane+ products; yield and reliability challenges in photonics.
Geopolitical risks given manufacturing in Taiwan/China and US-China tech tensions.

thesisSections.coreThesis: Applied Optoelectronics is a levered optical-components bet on AI clusters needing more bandwidth, more transceivers, and better power-per-bit as data movement becomes a binding constraint. The simple view is that AAOI is a volatile optical module supplier tied to customer cycles. The thesis view is that AI data-center scaling pushes optical content per cluster higher and makes vertical integration in lasers, components, and modules more valuable. It offers direct exposure to 400G/800G/1.6T optical networking demand. Vertical integration can matter if laser/component supply becomes tight. Hyperscaler relationships provide validation, though also concentration risk. It is more levered than diversified photonics leaders.
thesisSections.currentView: AAOI is positioned as a higher-beta expression of the optical interconnect bottleneck. Demand for higher-speed optical modules is growing as AI clusters scale, and the company's vertical integration in lasers and components provides potential margin and supply advantages during tight markets.
thesisSections.dissentingView: Customer concentration drives boom/bust revenue. Larger competitors such as Coherent, Lumentum, Broadcom, or Chinese suppliers could capture share. Price erosion could offset volume growth. AI optics demand could shift toward architectures where AAOI has weaker positioning. Manufacturing yield or reliability issues could impair hyperscaler trust.
evidence: It offers direct exposure to 400G/800G/1.6T optical networking demand.
Vertical integration can matter if laser/component supply becomes tight.
Hyperscaler relationships provide validation, though also concentration risk.
It is more levered than diversified photonics leaders.
AI data-center scaling is increasing optical content per cluster, favoring specialists with vertical integration.
risks: Customer concentration drives boom/bust revenue.
Larger competitors such as Coherent, Lumentum, Broadcom, or Chinese suppliers capture share.
Price erosion offsets volume growth.
AI optics demand shifts toward architectures where AAOI has weaker positioning.
Manufacturing yield or reliability issues impair hyperscaler trust.
Major hyperscaler programs are delayed, lost, or repriced.
Gross margin fails to improve despite AI optics demand.
thesisSections.investmentImplications: AAOI is a higher-beta expression of the optical interconnect bottleneck. It should be sized and reviewed as a volatile supplier, not as a broad semiconductor compounder. Keep customer concentration and product-cycle risk visible at all times. Tie upside to specific optical speed and AI cluster demand, not generic AI optimism. Monitor hyperscaler program wins, margin trends, and technology transitions closely. Suitable for higher-risk satellite positions within the optics theme.

profileSummary.oneLiner: AMD is the scaled x86 CPU and accelerator challenger to Intel and NVIDIA across PCs, servers, embedded systems, and AI accelerators.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: Bull case: Chiplet design expertise enabling cost-effective high-performance products. EPYC gaining traction in data centers. Instinct GPUs and ROCm software improving as alternative to CUDA. Strong position in AI accelerators, CPUs for training/inference clusters (see 2026-04-15 - Training Data Centers.md, 2026-04-15 - Inference Data Centers). Multiple foundry relationships but primarily TSMC. Benefits from overall AI infrastructure boom detailed across all data center theses.
keyRisks: NVIDIA's software moat (CUDA) makes GPU adoption harder.
Lags in some AI performance metrics.
Cyclical exposure to PC and broader semi downturns.
Competition from custom ASICs by hyperscalers.

thesisSections.coreThesis: AMD is the scaled alternative compute platform to NVIDIA and Intel, with upside if AI customers diversify accelerators and if CPUs remain essential to inference-heavy data-center architectures. The simple view is that AMD is a second-place GPU company chasing NVIDIA. The thesis view is that AMD does not need to beat NVIDIA everywhere. It can win as the open, cost-effective, high-performance alternative across EPYC CPUs, Instinct accelerators, adaptive silicon, and chiplet design. EPYC CPUs are important for data-center and inference orchestration. Instinct GPUs give customers a second source against NVIDIA. Chiplet design and TSMC access keep AMD competitive in performance per dollar. Xilinx/adaptive products broaden the embedded and heterogeneous compute surface.
thesisSections.currentView: AMD is a challenger and diversification holding, not the core AI platform. It is making progress in data-center but must prove software maturity and real production adoption to convert design wins into sustained revenue.
thesisSections.dissentingView: CUDA and NVIDIA's platform moat remain too strong for broad share gains. ROCm/software maturity may continue to lag customer needs. Custom ASICs from hyperscalers could take the workloads AMD hoped to win. PC/gaming cyclicality could offset data-center growth. Gross margins may stay structurally below the platform leader.
evidence: EPYC CPUs are important for data-center and inference orchestration.
Instinct GPUs give customers a second source against NVIDIA.
Chiplet design and TSMC access keep AMD competitive in performance per dollar.
Xilinx/adaptive products broaden the embedded and heterogeneous compute surface.
AMD provides a credible open alternative that appeals to customers seeking diversification from single-vendor risk.
risks: CUDA and NVIDIA's platform moat remain too strong.
ROCm/software maturity lags customer needs.
Custom ASICs take the workloads AMD hoped to win.
PC/gaming cyclicality offsets data-center growth.
Gross margins stay structurally below the platform leader.
Instinct design wins fail to convert into revenue.
ROCm remains a blocker for enterprise or hyperscaler adoption.
thesisSections.investmentImplications: AMD is a challenger and diversification holding. It should be judged by data-center share gains, software maturity (especially ROCm), and customer adoption in real production workloads. Track CPU and GPU theses separately. Compare AMD to the specific workloads it can actually win, not to NVIDIA's entire platform. Size as a satellite position for those seeking exposure to compute diversification.

profileSummary.oneLiner: Canadian Solar is a global solar and battery-storage company with module manufacturing, battery storage products, and project-development exposure through Recurrent Energy.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: Canadian Solar sits in the messy but strategically important solar-plus-storage value chain. The company is exposed to commodity solar module pressure, but also to project development, battery storage systems, and the broader need for more power supply as grids and data centers compete for electricity.
keyRisks: Solar module oversupply and pricing pressure.
Tariffs, trade policy, and China-linked supply-chain risk.
Project finance and working-capital complexity.
Debt burden and asset monetization timing.
Recurrent Energy value may remain underrecognized or poorly monetized.

thesisSections.coreThesis: Canadian Solar is a cheap and messy solar-plus-storage optionality bet where the upside comes less from commodity modules and more from project development, Recurrent Energy, battery storage, and the market eventually valuing power infrastructure scarcity.
thesisSections.dissentingView: The simple view is that CSIQ is a low-multiple, low-quality solar module company in a brutally oversupplied industry. The thesis view is that the market may be underpricing the value of Recurrent Energy, battery storage integration, and the ability to develop and monetize solar/storage projects when power availability becomes a strategic asset.
evidence: It combines module manufacturing with solar project development and storage.
Recurrent Energy gives it asset-development optionality, not just manufacturing exposure.
Battery storage links the company to grid reliability and data-center power constraints.
Valuation may already reflect a lot of solar-cycle pain.
risks: Module oversupply and China-linked pricing pressure destroy margins.
Trade policy, tariffs, or forced-labor scrutiny disrupt supply chains.
Recurrent Energy value remains trapped or poorly monetized.
Debt and project-finance complexity obscure true economics.
Solar remains a structurally poor industry despite growth.
thesisSections.investmentImplications: CSIQ is not a clean quality compounder. It is a contrarian optionality position that needs a clear review around storage backlog, Recurrent monetization, leverage, and whether margins can survive the solar downcycle.
thesisSections.whatWouldChangeMyMind: - Recurrent Energy fails to raise, sell, or recycle capital on attractive terms. - Storage growth does not offset module margin pressure. - Debt or working capital stress rises. - Trade/policy risk worsens enough to impair access to core markets.

profileSummary.oneLiner: DRAM is Roundhill’s actively managed memory-stock ETF, designed as a concentrated vehicle for owning the AI memory bottleneck through global HBM, DRAM, NAND, and storage leaders.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: - First true pure-play memory ETF in a market flooded with broad semiconductor funds. - Directly captures the secular memory bandwidth bottleneck that is now the primary constraint on AI training and inference scaling. - Efficient way to own the full memory stack (HBM leaders, DRAM, NAND) without single-stock risk. - Launched April 2026 — perfectly timed for the next leg of AI infrastructure buildout. This is the cleanest expression of the new Memory Bottleneck sub-thesis.
keyRisks: Rapid memory oversupply (especially if new fabs come online faster than expected).
Major advance in in-memory computing or optical interconnects that reduces the need for high-bandwidth memory.
Regulatory or geopolitical shock that disrupts the memory supply chain (Taiwan/Korea exposure).
ETF fails to attract sufficient assets and becomes illiquid.

thesisSections.coreThesis: DRAM is the cleanest portfolio vehicle for the view that memory has become a strategic bottleneck in AI infrastructure, especially as inference shifts more value toward HBM, DRAM, NAND, SSDs, and storage-heavy architectures.
thesisSections.dissentingView: The simple view is that memory remains a brutally cyclical commodity. The thesis view is that AI demand changes the customer base, contracting behavior, product mix, and strategic scarcity of memory. Cyclicality does not disappear, but the best memory suppliers may see longer periods of tight supply and better pricing power than the old DRAM cycle would imply.
risks: Memory supply expands faster than AI demand, recreating a classic oversupply cycle.
ETF liquidity remains poor because the fund is new and AUM fails to scale.
Swap structure, concentration, or non-U.S. exposure creates tracking or tax complexity.
AI architecture improves enough to reduce memory intensity per unit of useful inference.
thesisSections.investmentImplications: This is a core thematic basket, not a single-company operating bet. Add when memory scarcity evidence is improving but the market is treating memory as a commodity cycle. Trim if pricing power peaks, AUM/liquidity disappoints, or the fund drifts away from pure memory exposure.
thesisSections.whatWouldChangeMyMind: - HBM order books loosen materially across SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron. - Inference architectures shift away from large memory hierarchies. - DRAM ETF liquidity remains too thin for the desired position size. - The fund's holdings become too broad to express the memory bottleneck cleanly.

thesisSections.dissentingView: The simple view is that AI infrastructure is mostly GPUs. The stronger thesis is that as clusters scale, the bottlenecks migrate toward data movement, memory bandwidth, optical links, Ethernet, CXL, custom ASICs, and platform integration. Marvell sits in that second layer.

Existing Paul thesis work emphasizes optical DSPs, SerDes, Ethernet, custom ASICs/XPUs, CXL, and memory disaggregation.
risks: Broadcom or NVIDIA captures more of the AI connectivity stack.
Hyperscalers internalize more silicon design.
AI capex digestion pauses and custom silicon ramps slow.
Celestial AI / XConn integration does not produce meaningful product or revenue impact.
Customer concentration rises faster than operating leverage.

While the New York fab has been delayed, near-term HBM capacity ramps in existing fabs and partnerships should still deliver strong growth through 2027. HBM capacity, customer qualification, power efficiency, advanced packaging, and supply commitments may matter more than generic wafer additions. profileSummary.oneLiner: NVIDIA is the dominant AI accelerator and accelerated-computing platform company across GPUs, networking, software, and increasingly full-stack AI infrastructure.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: Bull case: NVIDIA's near-monopoly in high-performance AI compute (80-95% market share in AI accelerators) combined with its CUDA moat creates an incredibly sticky platform. The shift to AI training and inference has created a multi-year capex supercycle from hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META) and sovereign AI initiatives. Blackwell (B200/GB200) architecture delivers massive performance gains. Expansion into full stack (CPU, networking via Mellanox, software, Omniverse, robotics, autonomous vehicles, consumer A...
keyRisks: Extreme valuation dependent on continued AI hype and capex; any slowdown in hyperscaler spending could cause sharp correction.
Competition intensifying: AMD MI series, custom ASICs from hyperscalers (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium/Inferentia, Microsoft Maia), Intel Gaudi, potential new entrants.
Geopolitical risks: US export restrictions to China (major market), Taiwan tensions (manufacturing via TSMC).
Supply chain constraints on advanced packaging, HBM memory, and power delivery.
Regulatory scrutiny on monopoly power in AI chips.

thesisSections.coreThesis: NVIDIA is the default owner of the AI compute platform because it controls not just chips, but the integrated hardware, networking, software, and developer ecosystem that makes frontier AI infrastructure productive. The simple view is that NVIDIA sells expensive GPUs into an AI capex cycle. The thesis view is that NVIDIA is an operating system for AI factories. GPUs matter, but CUDA, networking, systems design, software libraries, rack-scale architectures, and customer co-design are what sustain the moat. It benefits from training and inference demand and monetizes multiple bottlenecks: compute, networking, cluster design, and software. Its ecosystem makes customers reluctant to optimize only for chip price. It remains the reference architecture for hyperscalers, sovereign AI, enterprises, and robotics.
thesisSections.currentView: NVDA is the benchmark AI infrastructure holding. It is not the only bottleneck owner, but it remains the platform against which other AI infrastructure bets should be compared. The company continues to execute across the full stack while the AI buildout accelerates.
thesisSections.dissentingView: Hyperscaler custom silicon may capture more incremental growth than expected. AMD, Broadcom, or internal ASICs could compress pricing and margins. AI capex digestion could create a multiple reset even if long-term demand remains strong. Export controls, Taiwan concentration, and supply chain limits remain structural risks. Customers may increasingly split workloads across cheaper inference stacks.

thesisSections.investmentImplications: NVDA is the core benchmark position in AI infrastructure. Size it as the reference holding and evaluate all other AI bets relative to its platform strength. Watch the split between training, inference, networking, and software value capture each quarter. The position benefits from continued AI scaling but requires monitoring for signs of platform erosion or capex digestion. Avoid generic "AI winner" framing; focus on which specific bottlenecks NVIDIA continues to own and monetize.

profileSummary.oneLiner: Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, is a storage and data-management platform company whose ticker changed from PSTG to P on the NYSE in April 2026.
profileSummary.whyItMatters: - Critical layer in the inference storage stack. In agentic workloads with massive context reuse (98%+ KV-cache hit rates), the bottleneck has shifted from raw training compute to fast, durable, cost-effective persistent storage for KV blocks that don't fit in HBM/DRAM. Everpure's technology targets this exact warm/cold tier with high IOPS, low latency NAND/SSD solutions tailored for AI. - Fits directly into the AI Bottleneck Thesis. As power, memory bandwidth, and optical fabric get attention, the storage layer (...
keyRisks: Commoditization of AI storage: If NAND manufacturers (MU, Samsung, SK Hynix) integrate AI-specific features directly, Everpure becomes redundant. Exit trigger.
Optical/near-memory breakthroughs that dramatically reduce the need for large persistent tiers. Trim trigger.
Execution risk on new AI-specific product line. Delayed shipments or poor real-world performance in production clusters. Trim trigger.

thesisSections.coreThesis: Investment in data platform companies enabling AI workloads represents a key layer in the AI infrastructure stack. Everpure is positioned at the intersection of storage, data management, and AI workload enablement, where the ability to ingest, store, and serve massive datasets efficiently becomes a bottleneck as model training and agentic inference scale. The thesis is that specialized data platforms that optimize for AI access patterns and integration with the broader training and inference fabric will capture durable value as the industry moves beyond generic cloud storage.
thesisSections.currentView: The company is building capabilities in data platform technologies tailored for AI. Demand for efficient, high-performance data infrastructure is rising with the growth of training runs and real-time inference workloads.
thesisSections.dissentingView: Generic cloud providers or hyperscaler internal platforms may satisfy most AI data needs, limiting the addressable market for specialized vendors. Execution on product-market fit and scaling sales could prove challenging in a competitive landscape.
evidence: Focus on storage and data platform technologies optimized for AI workloads.
Alignment with the Storage and Data Platform industry thesis.
Growing need for performant data layers as AI datasets and model requirements expand.
risks: Hyperscalers and major cloud providers continue to dominate data infrastructure for AI.

The integration of perception, planning, actuation, and energy gives Tesla a structural position in the physical layer of the AGI future that few others can replicate at scale.
thesisSections.currentView: Tesla is advancing on multiple fronts simultaneously: FSD continues to improve toward unsupervised autonomy and robotaxi networks, Optimus prototypes are progressing toward useful humanoid labor, and the energy business is scaling Megapack deployments that both support the grid and enable AI data center power needs. profileSummary.oneLiner: High-speed connectivity and signal integrity company focused on AI data center infrastructure, particularly PCIe, CXL, and Ethernet retimers and switches.

thesisSections.coreThesis: Astera Labs occupies a critical but often overlooked position in the AI infrastructure stack. As training and inference clusters scale to tens of thousands of accelerators, the physical challenges of moving data reliably at high speeds become first-order constraints. ALAB's retimers, PCIe/CXL controllers, and Ethernet solutions solve signal integrity problems that would otherwise limit cluster performance and density. The thesis is that connectivity and I/O scale faster than compute itself in large deployments, giving specialized players like Astera a leveraged position in the buildout. The market tends to focus on the obvious GPU and foundry winners, but the variant perception is that the "invisible" layers—high-speed serial links, retiming, and open standards for disaggregation—will determine which architectures actually get built at hyperscale.
thesisSections.currentView: ALAB has secured design wins with major hyperscalers and GPU providers and is seeing rapid revenue growth directly tied to the AI infrastructure buildout. Its technology leadership in retimer and connectivity ASICs positions it well as clusters demand ever-higher bandwidth and lower latency interconnects.
thesisSections.dissentingView: The primary counter is that larger, more diversified players such as Broadcom or NVIDIA's internal teams will capture the high-value connectivity layers, or that hyperscalers will increasingly design their own silicon for these functions. Cyclical pauses in AI CapEx could also delay or reduce demand for ALAB's products, and customer concentration means any single relationship loss would be material.
evidence: Strong design wins with major hyperscalers and GPU providers
Rapid revenue growth tied to AI infrastructure buildout
Technology leadership in retimer and connectivity ASICs

AI CapEx cycles are inherently lumpy; spending pauses or digestion periods could create sharp revenue volatility.
If alternative architectures or co-packaged optics reduce the need for discrete retimers and connectivity chips, the thesis weakens.
thesisSections.investmentImplications: ALAB is best held as a watching or satellite position within the broader AI Connectivity Bottleneck thesis. It offers higher-beta exposure to the data-movement bottleneck than more diversified names. Monitor design-win announcements, revenue ramps, and hyperscaler capex commentary closely. Add on pullbacks associated with temporary AI spending pauses, but size appropriately given the concentration and cyclical risks. The base case implies strong CAGR as cluster sizes drive higher connectivity content per accelerator, but position sizing must reflect the execution and customer risks.

thesisSections.coreThesis: Snowflake provides the elastic, governed, multi-cloud data platform that enterprises increasingly rely on as the central repository and collaboration layer for AI data workloads. Snowflake's architecture (separation of storage/compute, time travel, secure data sharing, Snowpark for in-platform development) positions it well to serve as the "data operating system" for both analytics and the emerging generation of data-hungry AI applications and agents. Both address the "data problem" that becomes acute when organizations try to productio...
thesisSections.currentView: Snowflake has strong product-market fit in the cloud data platform category and is successfully layering AI capabilities on top of its core strengths. Its consumption model aligns incentives with growing AI data workloads. The network effects from data sharing and the marketplace create data gravity that is difficult for alternatives to displace quickly. As enterprises move more AI experimentation and production workloads onto governed cloud data platforms, Snowflake is one of the best-positioned pure-play beneficiaries.
thesisSections.dissentingView: Databricks and hyperscaler offerings will capture the majority of new AI data workloads due to better integration with their ML ecosystems, lower cost for certain workloads, or stronger existing relationships. Snowflake's core data warehouse strengths matter less in a world dominated by lakehouse architectures and vector-native systems. Margin pressure from AI compute intensity and competitive pricing will limit profitability even if revenue grows.

theses.label: Access to Interconnection Energy
theses.summary: The energy bottleneck for AI is not solely about total generation capacity. It is about whether a specific load can access usable, interconnected, deliverable power at the required location and on the required timeline. Interconnection queues, transmission constraints, transformer shortages, permitting, and utility processes are the practical gates between theoretical power and energized AI clusters.

theses.label: AGI Wins
theses.summary: AGI will be the most important technology of the 21st century, but it will not arrive as a single dramatic event or a smooth curve of capability improvement. It will arrive as a series of increasingly violent collisions between exponential algorithmic progress and the stubborn realities of the physical world. The core bet is this: sufficiently powerful AI systems will be built, and once built, they will be deployed at massive scale. theses.label: AI Connectivity Bottleneck
theses.summary: As AI clusters scale, the bottleneck shifts from simply owning accelerators to making accelerators, memory, custom silicon, storage, and racks behave like one usable system. The investable constraint is high-speed connectivity: Ethernet, PCIe/CXL, retimers, switches, SerDes, optical DSPs, fabric software, and custom interconnect silicon.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Bottleneck Thesis > AI Connectivity Bottleneck

theses.label: AI Distribution and Aggregation
theses.summary: In the era of abundant intelligence, the decisive battle is not who trains the best foundation model but who aggregates demand—who controls the interface between paying customers (consumers, enterprises, workflows) and the supply of intelligence. The winners will be the platforms that already own distribution, attention, commerce, or vertical workflows and that embed AI to deepen lock-in and data advantages. New pure-AI aggregators are possible but face the classic cold-start problem against incumbents with existing relationships.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Industries 3.0 > AI Distribution and Aggregation

theses.label: BESS as Grid Economics Enhancer
theses.summary: Battery energy storage systems (BESS) are not merely backup power. They are a grid-economic optimizer that improves the value of generation, relieves transmission and distribution constraints, enhances load flexibility for data centers, and accelerates time-to-power for AI infrastructure. As volatility, renewable penetration, and AI load growth rise in tandem, storage becomes a high-leverage tool for monetizing spreads, deferring capex, and unlocking capacity.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Bottleneck Thesis > Energy Bottleneck > BESS as Grid Economics Enhancer

theses.summary: AI will win, but victory will be determined by successfully navigating a series of shifting physical and human bottlenecks. The durable edge is to identify and own the most priceable, persistent bottleneck at each stage while avoiding supply chain whiplash.

theses.label: Compute Bottleneck
theses.summary: In the AGI race, leading-edge compute remains the scarce, high-leverage input that determines which labs can iterate fastest. The bottleneck is structural and multi-layered—accelerators, advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory attach, networking fabric, and the software stack that turns silicon into usable training and inference capacity.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Bottleneck Thesis > Compute Bottleneck

theses.label: Cybersecurity (in the AI Era)
theses.summary: In the Industries 3.0 era, abundant intelligence dramatically expands the attack surface while simultaneously creating new defensive capabilities. The companies that build the platforms for securing AI systems, agents, data, and the expanded digital perimeter will capture significant value as the default "security operating system" for the AI economy.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Industries 3.0 > Cybersecurity (in the AI Era)

theses.label: Data (Platforms & Governance)
theses.summary: In the Industries 3.0 era, the companies that own the modern data platforms — unified semantic layers, governed data products, and the operating systems on which AI agents actually run — capture disproportionate value. These are not traditional data warehouses or lakes, but the new aggregation and governance layers required when intelligence becomes abundant and organizations need reliable, queryable, decision-grade data at scale.

theses.label: Data Center Build Out
theses.summary: If AGI wins, the world requires a sustained, multi-year buildout of intelligence infrastructure. Data centers are the factories that convert power, chips, memory, networking, cooling, data, and operations into useful intelligence. The investable thesis is that this buildout creates recurring, shifting bottlenecks across every layer of the stack, with durable value accruing to owners of the scarce inputs and systems-level integrators.
theses.thesisPath: AGI Wins > Data Center Build Out

Compute can be ordered faster than power can be permitted, generated, transmitted, and firmed. The labs and hyperscalers engaged in the AGI race will pay premiums and accept inferior unit economics for speed-to-power; this creates durable scarcity and optionality for those who control or enhance energy access.

"Just a Trade" is the explicit category for tactical, price-based, event-driven, opportunistic, or experimental holdings. Maintaining this separation protects the integrity of the core thesis portfolio and forces clarity on why capital is deployed.

theses.label: Memory Bottleneck
theses.summary: AI scaling—particularly the shift to massive inference, agentic workloads, and high-context reasoning—is now gated by memory bandwidth and HBM supply more than raw FLOPs alone. Memory has become the new oil of the intelligence era: structurally scarce, high-margin, and slow to expand.

theses.label: Optical Interconnect Bottleneck
theses.summary: As AI clusters scale to hundreds of thousands of accelerators, electrical copper interconnects hit hard physical limits on bandwidth, latency, and power. Optical interconnects—via silicon photonics, co-packaged optics (CPO), and InP-based lasers—become the only viable path for both intra-rack and inter-rack communication, creating a new structural bottleneck and supply chain layer.
